title: M/S Ram Finance Company vs . Sanjay Taneja on 12 August, 2026
full_text: M/S Ram Finance Company vs . Sanjay Taneja on 12 August, 2026 IN THE COURT OF Ms. AASTHA SHARMA, LD. JMFC (N.I. Act)-03, SOUTH-EAST DISTRICT, SAKET COURTS COMPLEX: DELHI M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja CC No. 15415/2019 U/S 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 1. CNR number DLSE020344432019 2. Name of the complainant M/s Ram Finance Company, Through its Authorised Representative Sh. Ram Asra Mal Bhutani, Through its SPA Holder, Sh. Ashok Kumar Bhutani R/o D-126, East of Kailash, New Delhi- 110065. 3. Name of the accused person(s), parentage Sh. Sanjay Taneja, & residential address CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 1 of 14 Digitally signed AASTHA by AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:55:28 +0530 Proprietor of M/s Taneja Paints and Hardware Store. S/o Late Sh. Govind Lal Taneja, R/o 198/1 Ramesh Market, East of Kailash, New Delhi- 110065. 4. Offence complained of or proved U/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 5. Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty and claimed trial 6. Final Judgment/order Conviction 7. Date of judgment/order 12.08.2026. Date of Institution : 05.08.2019 Date of Reserving Judgment/Order : 13.07.2026 Date of Pronouncement of Judgment/Order : 12.08.2026. ARGUING COUNSELS: Ld. Counsel for the complainant : Sh. Ashok K. Vadhera Ld. Counsel for the Accused : Sh. Mehmood Parcha JUDGMENT CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 2 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:55:55 +0530 1. Vide this judgment, this Court shall dispose of the present complaint filed by the complainant M/s Ram Finance Company (hereinafter referred to as "complainant") against M/s Taneja Paints & Hardware Store through its proprietor Sh. Sanjay Taneja (hereinafter referred to as the "accused") under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 read with Section 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as " NI Act "). Brief facts of the case: 2. It is the case of the complainant, A. That, the complainant had friendly relation with the accused since 2013 and the accused requested the complainant to provide the necessary finances of Rs. 20,00,000/- in the month of August 2017, Rs. 20,00,000/- in the month of February 2018 and Rs. 20,00,000/- in the month of April 2018 and promised to repay the same alongwith interest in 20 monthly installments. That, the complainant gave the accused loan of Rs. 20,00,000/- vide cheque no. 647449 dated 09.08.2017, Rs. 20,00,000/- vide cheque no. 030257 dated 16.12.2018, Rs. 20,00,000/- vide cheque no. 030261 dated 17.04.2018, all drawn on Bank of India, East of Kailash Branch, New Delhi in the presence of his son Ashok Kumar Bhutani. B. That, the accused no. 1 then issued 20 post dated cheques bearing no. 028276 to 028295; 20 post dated cheques bearing no. 033845 to 033865; 20 post dated cheques bearing no. 502256 to 502275, all in the sum of Rs. 1,30,000/- each (Rs. 1,00,000/- against the principal and Rs. 30,000/- towards interest on the principal amount), all drawn on IndusInd Bank, Lajpat Nagar, Delhi in favour of the complainant with the assurance that the same shall be honored on presentation. CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 3 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.08.12 16:56:00 +0530 C. That, upon assurance and representation of the accused, the complainant presented the said cheques before his bank Bank of India, East of Kailash Branch, New Delhi, however, three cheques bearing no. 033858 dated 14.04.2019, bearing no. 502268 dated 15.04.2019 and bearing no. 033859 dated 14.05.2019, all in the sum of Rs. 1,30,000/- were returned unpaid with remarks "Payment Stopped by Drawer" vide return memos dated 06.06.2019. D. In these circumstances, the complainant got issued a statutory legal demand notice to the accused person through his counsel, dated 20.06.2019, thereby requiring the accused person to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheques within a period of 15 days from the receipt of the said notice. The said notice under Sec. 138 of NI Act was sent to the accused person through Registered AD/Speed Post/Courier at their correct address. That despite service of the above stated notice of demand, the Accused person has deliberately and willfully failed to comply with the said notice of demand and has failed to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheque within the stipulated period of 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice. Consequently, this case was filed by the complainant against the accused persons, which was within the limitation period as laid down u/s 138 , NI Act. 3. In the pre-summoning evidence, the complainant through his SPA Holder examined himself on affidavit being Ex. CW1/A and relied on documents Ex. CW1/1 to Ex. CW1/15. 4. Upon prima facie consideration of the pre-summoning evidence, the accused no. 1 through its proprietor accused no. 2 was summoned. 5. Upon the appearance of the accused, notice under Section 251 CrPC was served upon him on 29.08.2022 to which he pleaded not guilty. The accused has CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 4 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:06 +0530 admitted his signatures on the cheques in question. The accused has denied any liability towards the complainant. The accused has further denied receiving the legal demand notice. 6. Vide a separate statement of accused, admissions and denials u/s 294 CrPC was recorded and witnesses 3, 4 and 5 from the list of complainant witnesses were dropped. 7. CW-1, CW-2 and CW-3 were examined-in-chief, cross-examined and discharged. Thereby, CE was closed vide order of this court. Accordingly, matter proceeded to the stage of recording the statement of the accused. 8. Statement of accused under Section 313 CrPC read with Section 281 CrPC was recorded on 19.08.2025 wherein the accused opted to lead defence evidence. DW-1 and DW-2 were examined in chief, cross-examined and discharged. Vide order of this court, DE was closed on 01.06.2026. 9. Thereafter, the matter was listed for final arguments. After hearing the final arguments from both sides, the matter was reserved for pronouncement of judgment. 10. It is well settled position of law that to constitute an offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the following ingredients are required to be fulfilled: I. drawing of the cheque by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker, II. The cheque was issued for payment to another person for discharge in whole/part any debt or liability; CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 5 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:11 +0530 III. Cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier. RBI in its notification DBOD.AML BC.No.47/14.01.001/2011-12 has reduced the aforesaid period from 6 months to 3 months. IV. Returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque; V. Giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of the receipt of information by the payee from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid demanding payment of the cheque amount; VI. Failure of the drawer to make payment to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, of the amount covered by the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the notice. The offence under Section 138 , NI Act is made out against the drawer of the cheque, only when all the aforementioned ingredients are fulfilled. 11. Analysing all the concerned provisions of law and various pronouncements in this regard, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Basalingappa v. Mudibasappa [AIR 2019 SC 1983] held that: I. Once the execution of cheque is admitted, Section 139 of the Act mandates that a presumption be drawn that the cheque in question was for the discharge of any debt or other liability. CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 6 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:21 +0530 II. The presumption under Section 139 is a rebuttable presumption and the onus is on the accused to raise the probable defence. The standard of proof for rebutting the presumption is that of preponderance of probabilities. III. To rebut the presumption, it is open for the accused to rely on evidence led by him or accused can also rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise a probable defence. Inference of preponderance of probabilities can be drawn not only from the materials brought on record by reference to the circumstances upon which they rely. IV. That it is not necessary for the accused to come in the witness box in support of his defence. Section 139 imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden. It is therefore implied that the law regarding the presumption for the offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the presumptions under Section 118(a) and Section 139 have to be compulsorily raised as soon as the execution of cheque by the accused is admitted or proved by the complainant and thereafter the burden is shifted upon the accused to prove otherwise. Appreciation of evidence and marshalling of facts: 12. Issuance of cheque: The complainant has filed on record the original cheques, i.e., bearing no. 033858 dated 14.04.2019 for Rs. 1,30,000/-, bearing no. 502268 dated 15.04.2019 for Rs. 1,30,000/- and bearing no. 033859 dated 14.05.2019 for Rs. 1,30,000/-, all drawn on IndusInd Bank, Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi (Ex. CW1/1, Ex. CW1/2 & Ex. CW1/3). In notice under Section 251 CrPC, the accused has admitted that the cheques in dispute belong to him. It is also not disputed that the cheques in question are not drawn on the account maintained by CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 7 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:26 +0530 the accused and it is impliedly admitted therefore that the accused is the drawer of the cheque. Therefore, ingredient number I stands fulfilled in the present case. 13. Presentment and dishonor of cheque: As per the RBI guidelines, it is essential for the cheque in question be to presented within a period of three months from the date on which they are drawn and the same be returned as unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque. In the case at hand, the cheque in question was returned vide return memos (Ex. CW1/4, Ex. CW1/5 & Ex. CW1/6) due to the reason "Payment Stopped by Drawer" By implication thereof, the cheques were presented within three months and the same were returned. Therefore, Ingredient number III & IV stand fulfilled in the present case. 14. Legal demand notice and payment by the accused thereof: The legal notice dated 20.06.2019 (Ex. CW1/7) was dispatched on 21.06.2019 vide Speed Post (Ex. CW1/8 & Ex. CW1/9), i.e., within 30 days of return of the bank memo indicating cheques in question being unpaid. The fact that the legal demand notice has made a clear and unambiguous demand for payment of the cheque in question is not disputed. The accused has denied the receiving of legal demand notice in notice u/s 251 CrPC. However, the address of the accused on DW-1 is the same as mentioned on the legal demand notice. Furthermore, as per the presumption raised under Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and Section 27 of General Clauses Act, if the legal demand notice is sent at the correct address, then the same shall be deemed to have been duly served, as per the precedent laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.C. Alavi Haji v. Palapetty Muhammed , (2007) 3 SCC (Cri). The ingredient number V is fulfilled by virtue of giving of legal demand notice CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 8 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA Date: SHARMA 2026.08.12 16:56:32 +0530 within 30 days from the bank return memo. The receipt of legal demand notice by the accused is deemed to be admitted as per the discussion above. 15. Moving on, it is not disputed that the accused has not made the payment of the cheque amount within 15 days of the receipt of legal demand notice. Therefore, ingredient number VI also stands fulfilled in the present case. Presumption under Section 118A read with Section 139 , NI Act 16. The NI Act raises two presumptions in favour of the holder of the cheque, i.e., complainant; firstly, with regard to the issuance of cheque for consideration, as contained in Section 118(a) and secondly, with regard to the fact that the holder of cheque received the same for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, as contained in Section 139 of the Act. These presumptions shall end only when the contrary is proved by the accused, that is, the cheque was not issued for consideration and in discharge of any debt or liability etc. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment titled Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan , (2010) 11 SCC 441 held that a reverse onus clause usually imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden and when an accused has to rebut the presumption under Section 139 , the standard of proof for doing so is that of "preponderance of probabilities". Therefore, if the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability, the prosecution can fail. It was further held that the accused can rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise such a defence and it is conceivable that in some cases the accused may not need to adduce evidence of his/her own. Once a probable defence is raised, then the onus is shifted to the complainant to establish that a legally enforceable liability existed in his CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 9 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:39 +0530 favour and the burden of proof on the complainant in this case is that of "beyond reasonable doubt." 17. The accused can rebut the presumption as raised under Section 138 , NI Act by: (a) putting forth his defence at the time of framing of notice u/s 251 CrPC; (b) cross-examining the complainant; (c) when statement of accused is recorded u/s 313 CrPC; (d) or by leading defence evidence, thereby demolishing the case of the complainant. Rebuttal of Presumption by Accused as to existence of legally enforceable debt 18. In light of the above discussion, since the accused has admitted to issuance of cheques, admitted the signatures on the cheques and legal notice has also been deemed to be served, what is left to be seen is whether the accused has been able to rebut the presumption against him, i.e., whether the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt? 19. In the present case, in order to discharge his initial burden to prove the abovementioned ingredients, the complainant relied upon the affidavit of the complainant being Ex. CW1/A and placed on record documents mentioned hereinbefore. The case of the complainant is that the accused had borrowed a sum of Rs. 60,00,000/- from the complainant, indicated by statement of accounts Ex. CW1/13 (Colly.) and Ex. CW3/1 which were to be repaid in equal installments of CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 10 ofDigitally 14 signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.08.12 16:56:44 +0530 Rs. 1,30,000/- for which the cheques in question were issued. The case of the complainant is that these cheques got dishonoured. Per Contra, the accused submits that he does not owe any liability towards the complainant. 20. The accused on one hand in his defence u/s 313 CrPC has stated that the complainant had approached him to invest in his business and the accused shall give him 25% of the earned profit and the loss shall be borne equally by both the parties and the cheques in question were issued by the accused to the complainant against the said profit in advance. The accused has further denied taking any loan from the complainant or making any interest payment to the complainant in his statement u/s 313 CrPC. On the other hand, the accused at the stage of DE has stated that the complainant used to advance loan on interest and take security cheque for each installment and the accused has paid Rs. 1,30,000/- for repayment of the said loan. The accused, however, has not placed any document on record to prove that he has repaid the amount as mentioned in the cheque in question to the complainant and has made mere contradictory statements to escape his liability. 21. The accused has later examined his accountant as DW-2 to corroborate his version as taken by the accused in DW-1. DW-2 has also admitted that the accused owes certain liability to the complainant, however he has not placed on record a statement of account or any other document to indicate the pending liability of the accused. DW-2 has rather corroborated the version of the complainant qua TDS deduction, thereby implying admission of loan transaction in question by the accused. 22. Ld. Counsel for the accused has further argued that the complainant has not examined their best witness, i.e., the complainant and therefore the consequential CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 11 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:50 +0530 benefit of the same has to be granted to the accused. Ld. Counsel for the accused further submits that since the complainant did not enter into the witness box and the SPA holder does not have personal knowledge of the facts of the case, therefore the case of the complainant is not proved. It is to be noted that Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of AC Narayanan v. State of Maharashtra (2014) 11 SCC 790, has held that filing of complaint petition u/s 138 , NI Act through power of attorney is perfectly legal and competent and the POA holder can depose and verify on oath to prove the contents of the complainant, if he had personally witnessed the transaction or had due knowledge about the material contents of the transaction. In the present case, the SPA holder Sh. Ashok Bhutani had mentioned in his affidavit that he is duly conversant with the facts of the present case and had knowledge of the present transaction. Furthermore, perusal of examination of the SPA holder as CW-1 clearly indicates that the SPA holder was aware about the material contents of the present loan transaction and was duly conversant of the facts of the case, in terms of the AC Narayanan (supra). Therefore, the argument of the accused that the complainant has not examined their best witness and therefore the case of the complainant is not proved is not a substantial defence and has no footing. 23. Furthermore, the defence of the accused is that the complainant was a money lender as per Punjab Registration of Money Lenders Act as he has been advancing loan to the accused since several years at interest rate and seeking security cheques for the same loan transaction. It is to be noted that the Punjab Registration of Money Lenders Act, 1939 does not define "money lenders" and advancing loan to one individual does not make the complainant a money lender. The accused has nowhere examined any other individual as a witness or placed on record any document which proves that the complainant used to regularly advance loans to CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 12 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:56:55 +0530 individuals at interest. Moreover, Punjab Registration of Money Lenders Act, 1939 also does not implicitly or explicitly bar proceedings u/s 138 , NI Act. Ld. Counsel for the accused has placed on record order of Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Santoshi v. Prashant Malik (Misc . App. No. 1176/2026 in SLP (CrL.) No. 5485/2024) wherein it was held that proceedings arising out of money lending transactions without an individual holding money lending license are against State Money Lending law and any civil or criminal proceeding arising out of them should be nipped in the bud. The present case deals with Section 138 , NI Act proceeding having a limited purview and if the issuance of the cheque and the signature on the cheque are admitted by the accused, then the presumption u/s 139 Act arises and the onus completely shifts upon the accused to rebut the presumption. The case relied upon by the Ld. Counsel of the accused deals with State Money Lending Law and therefore the same is not applicable in the present case. 24. In the present case, the accused has failed to even create any doubt, let alone discharging his burden of proof to rebut the presumption u/s 139 , NI Act. Further, the accused is obligated to set up a probable defence and not a possible defence, i.e., there should be some credible material or circumstance on record to show that the defence taken by the accused is a probable one. In the present case, firstly, the accused has not brought any witness on record nor brought any documentary evidence on record to substantiate his claims. It is the duty of the accused to punch holes in the story of the complainant which he has not been able to do. Secondly, the complainant has brought documentary evidence so as to prove his version of the story alongwith the benefit of presumption raised u/s 139 , NI Act in his favour. CC No. 15415/2019 M/s Ram Finance Company Vs. Sanjay Taneja Page 13 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.08.12 16:57:02 +0530 25. In light of the discussion above, this Court is of the view that the accused has not been able to rebut the presumption against him and therefore ingredient no. II has been fulfilled in the present case. Conclusion: 26. In view of the evidence adduced, documents put forth and arguments advanced by the parties and further in view of the above discussion, the court is of the considered view that accused Sanjay Taneja, proprietor of M/s Taneja Paints & Hardware Store is guilty of offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and accordingly, accused is hereby convicted under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 27. Copy of this judgment be given to the convict free of cost as per rules. PRONOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA TODAY ON 12th August, 2026.
